architecture.mechanism: Multi-agent reinforcement learning–based task offloading that jointly optimizes task attributes, queue load, communication link quality, and computing resources to avoid overload and communication failures under dynamic, high-mobility conditions.
architecture.intervention: Deploy an on-vehicle multi-agent reinforcement learning controller on the transmission control unit that continuously monitors transmission torque-converter slip, shift-solenoid queue load, clutch-pack pressure, and communication link health with the powertrain/ABS/ECU nodes, dynamically redistributing shift-command processing and predictive shift scheduling to prevent clutch/solenoid overload and electromechanical command loss.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced hard shifting and slipping under normal city driving by avoiding transmission-controller overload and cross-zone communication-induced shift command failures, extending transmission life and supporting smooth gear transitions.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument two otherwise identical vehicles on identical city-driving cycles; compare transmissions monitored by the MATPPO-T-style offloading controller versus a baseline transmission controller, and reject the mechanism if the controlled unit does not show statistically significant reduction (e.g., >30% lower) in slip events, hard-shift counts, and premature failure incidence before 5,000 miles.
